test_title: PYST 21: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 18 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the legislative allocation of cooperative societies in the Constitution of India?

options.text: It is a subject in the State List
It falls under the Residuary (Union) List.
It is a subject in the Union List.
It is a subject in the Concurrent List.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is a subject in the State List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Constitution of India**, subjects are divided into three lists: the **Union List**, **State List**, and **Concurrent List**, as per the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• **Cooperative societies** are specifically listed as Item 32 in the **State List**. Therefore, the state governments have the exclusive authority to legislate on this matter.
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011**, added a new part (Part IXB) to the Constitution, which deals with the working of cooperative societies. However, the legislative domain remains under the **State List**.
 
• The amendment also added the word “**cooperatives**” to Article 19(1)(c), ensuring that people have the right to form cooperative societies as part of their fundamental rights.
 
• **Statement 1:** "It is a subject in the State List" is correct, as cooperative societies fall under the exclusive legislative authority of the states.
 
• **Statement 2:** "It falls under the Residuary (Union) List" is incorrect because cooperative societies are explicitly mentioned in the State List, and residuary subjects are those not enumerated in any list.
 
• **Statement 3:** "It is a subject in the Union List" is incorrect, as cooperative societies are not included in the Union List.
 
• **Statement 4:** "It is a subject in the Concurrent List" is incorrect, as cooperative societies are not enumerated in the Concurrent List.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State List:**

 
 
• It consists of **66 subjects** under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution.
 
• State governments have exclusive legislative power on subjects listed in the State List, such as **police**, **public health**, **agriculture**, and **cooperative societies**.
 
 
 
• **97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011:**
 
 
• This amendment emphasized the importance of **cooperative societies** and their autonomy.
 
• It added **Part IXB** to the Constitution, laying down provisions for the effective functioning of cooperative societies.
 
• The amendment also inserted **Article 43B**, which directs states to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, and professional management of cooperative societies.
 
 
 
• **Union List:**
 
 
• The Union List consists of **97 subjects**, including matters of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• Only the Parliament has the exclusive power to legislate on subjects in the Union List.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The Concurrent List consists of **47 subjects**, where both the Union and State legislatures can legislate, such as criminal law, marriage, education, etc.
 
• In case of conflict between Union and State laws, the Union law prevails.
 
 
 
• **Residuary Powers:**
 
 
• Residuary subjects are those not enumerated in the Union, State, or Concurrent Lists.
 
• According to **Article 248**, the power to legislate on residuary subjects lies exclusively with the Parliament.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cooperative Movement in India:**

 
 
• The cooperative movement in India began in the late **19th century** with the enactment of the **Cooperative Credit Societies Act, 1904**.
 
• Cooperatives play a significant role in various sectors like agriculture, banking, housing, and dairy production.
 
• Examples include **Amul** (dairy cooperative) and **IFFCO** (fertilizer cooperative).
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court Judgment:**
 
 
• In **2021**, the Supreme Court ruled that certain provisions of the **97th Constitutional Amendment** were unconstitutional as they encroached upon the domain of states.
 
• The judgment reaffirmed that cooperative societies primarily fall under the **State List**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Cooperative Societies:**
 
 
• Cooperative societies promote **economic welfare**, encourage **self-help**, and foster **mutual aid** among their members.
 
• They are pivotal in areas like rural credit, marketing of agricultural produce, and housing.
